question: Which of the following movements is also known as the 'Salt Satyagraha'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Civil Disobedience Movement**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Salt Satyagraha**, also known as the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, was a significant phase of the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was led by **Mahatma Gandhi** in March 1930 to protest against the British monopoly on salt production and sales.
 
• The movement began with the historic **Dandi March**, where Gandhi and his followers marched from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi in Gujarat to make salt from seawater.
 
• This act of defiance against British laws sparked widespread participation across India and became a symbol of resistance against colonial rule.
 
• The **Civil Disobedience Movement** aimed to achieve **Purna Swaraj** (complete self-rule) and involved the refusal to obey certain laws, demands, and commands of the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement** (1920-1922) was another major movement led by Gandhi, urging Indians to withdraw from British institutions.
 
• The **Quit India Movement** (1942) was a mass protest demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• The **Indian Self Rule Movement** refers to the broader struggle for independence, encompassing various movements and efforts to achieve self-governance.
 
• The **Salt Satyagraha** was a pivotal event that galvanized Indian society and gained international attention, highlighting the injustices of British colonial rule.
